name: Fortio
what_it_is: Fortio is Istio's open-source load testing tool and library (written in Go) that runs at a specified QPS, records latency histograms, and calculates percentiles. It ships as a CLI, an echo/ping server, a gRPC server, TCP/UDP echo servers, a web UI, and a REST API for triggering and inspecting runs.
measurement: latency histogram with configurable resolution (default 1 ms buckets)
configurable percentiles (default p50, p75, p90, p99, p99.9)
error counts and HTTP non-2xx status breakdown
comparative multi-run graphs (min, avg, median, p75, p99, p99.9, max)
access log (JSON or InfluxDB line format)
configuration: -qps: target queries per second (0 = max speed)
-n: fixed number of calls instead of duration
-echo-server-default-params: default query-string for the echo server (delay, status, size, close, header, gzip)
-connection-reuse min:max: randomized connection reuse threshold per thread
-uniform / -nocatchup: call distribution and QPS ceiling controls
-dns-method: DNS round-robin strategy (cached-rr, rnd, first, rr)
-config-dir / -config-port: dynamic flag watching and live reconfiguration
-sync URL / -sync-interval: pull remote JSON result index at startup and on schedule
-loglevel: Debug / Verbose / Info / Warning / Error / Critical / Fatal
fault_injection: delay= query param: inject latency with probability distribution (e.g. delay=150us:10,2ms:5,0.5s:1)
status= query param: return non-200 HTTP status codes with probability distribution (e.g. status=503:5,429:1)
size= query param: vary response payload size with probability distribution
close= query param: close socket after a fraction of requests (e.g. close=5.3 for ~5.3%)
-echo-server-default-params: set server-wide defaults for all of the above without requiring client query args
-abort-on: abort the entire load test run if a specific HTTP status code (or -1 for socket error) is encountered
modes: server: combined echo + gRPC + redirect + proxy + web UI + REST API server
report: read-only result browsing and graphing server
curl: single HTTP fetch for debugging
nc: single TCP or UDP connection (netcat-like)
proxies: run only the -M and -P configured proxies
script: interactive or file-based grol scripting (e.g. ramp-up load scripts)
version / buildinfo: print version and build metadata
constraints: Docker image is under 6 MB; minimal external dependencies — not suitable as a replacement for full observability stacks
Fast HTTP/1.1 client does not support h2/h2c; HTTP/2 requires -stdclient or -h2 flag, which is slower
UDP echo server uses a single goroutine by default; -udp-async enables concurrent replies but adds complexity
Connection reuse, keepalive, and half-close options only apply to the fast HTTP/1.1 client, not stdclient
Result JSON files are stored flat in a single data directory; no built-in database or time-series backend
Fan-out proxy (-M) mirrors requests in parallel by default; serial mode (-multi-serial-mode) serialises them, increasing latency
grol scripting engine is embedded and simplified (not full Go); complex orchestration logic may hit language limits
Maximum echo-server response payload is capped at -maxpayloadsizekb (default 256 KB)
TLS mutual authentication (-mtls) requires a custom CA certificate; standard internet CAs only work for outbound client connections

docker_services.note: Single multi-architecture image (linux/amd64, linux/arm64, linux/ppc64le, linux/s390x); no official docker-compose.yaml found in the repository

notable_absences: No built-in distributed/coordinated load generation across multiple agents
No Prometheus metrics endpoint by default (pprof available, but not a /metrics scrape target)
No docker-compose.yaml in the repository — single-container usage only
No native WebSocket load testing support
No built-in CI result diffing or SLO pass/fail thresholds (must be scripted via grol or external tooling)
